title: Model Photos Without a Photoshoot | AIVideosUGC
description: Get model photos without a photoshoot: photograph the garment flat, pick an adult look and setting, then check the fit before posting. Learn how and try it.
h1: How to Get Model Photos Without a Photoshoot
lead: You can get model photos without a photoshoot by photographing the garment flat, picking an adult look you can save and reuse, then checking the fit details before you post.
secondary_keywords: on-model photos from a flat lay
summary: A flat or hanger photo becomes an on-model image for new arrivals and short runs, after you check neckline, length, print, and hardware.

paras: When a flat photo is enough, how to shoot the garment, how to save a look, how jewelry differs, what to compare, how a batch run works, the three steps, and the other photo tools on the same account.
sections.alt: Adult man with short silver hair wearing a plain gray hoodie outside a storefront.

sections.h2: Visualize Your Products on an AI Model
paras: Model photos without a photoshoot suit new arrivals, short runs, and print-on-demand, when booking a person, a photographer, and a day is hard to justify.

You upload a photo of the piece, pick who wears it and where, and get an image of it being worn. They do not prove exact fit. A generated image cannot tell a shopper how a medium will sit on their body, so keep the size chart and the measurements on the listing.
sections.alt: Adult woman with short copper hair wearing a plain gray hoodie on an autumn city sidewalk.

sections.h2: Launch New Arrivals Without a Studio Day
paras: Lay the piece flat or hang it on a bare wall, shoot straight on in daylight, and steam wrinkles out first. A new drop can go on an adult look once that photo exists.

Creases in the source photo can turn into odd folds on the person. Get the whole garment in frame, including sleeves, hem, and collar. Turn a print toward the camera. Photograph each color separately. A generated color may not match your dye. For a wider set of stills that are not on a person, the [AI product photo generator](page:photo-hub) covers angles and detail.
sections.alt: Hands smooth a plain gray hoodie beside a wooden hanger on a light surface.

sections.h2: Keep One Look Across Every Channel
paras: Yes. Save the adult look, the pose, and the scene, then pick that saved look on the next piece so the face stays put.

Use the same saved look on the product page, a [marketplace listing](page:plat-amazon), and an [Instagram post](page:plat-instagram) so the shop does not jump between people. If you skip the saved look and describe someone new, the face can change. Repeat the age, hair, and build when you want the pictures to feel related. On the product page, put a clean product shot first and the on-model images after it.

sections.h2: Can I make AI jewelry model photos the same way?
paras: Yes. Use a close, sharp photo of the piece on a plain surface, with the clasp, stones, and chain in focus. Save the look if the next piece should sit on the same person.

A line such as "close profile, short hair tucked back, soft window light, the earring clearly visible" is enough. In the result, count the stones, check the clasp, and see whether a necklace falls where that length should sit. Small pieces depend more on a crisp source photo than clothing does.

sections.h2: Show the Drape, Then Check the Real Piece
paras: The photo can show how cloth hangs, where a print sits, and how a neckline reads on a body. It still does not prove a size. Keep the size chart on the listing.

Compare each image with the real piece. Check the neckline, sleeve and hem length, where the print sits, the button count, and which side the zipper is on. Stripes and checks should line up the way they do on the garment. Hands and hairlines deserve a second look. If anything does not match, make a new version rather than posting one that is close enough. Plan two or three images per piece: one full view, one closer crop of the cloth or the stone, and one in a setting that fits how it is worn. Each image is 24 credits, and the cost is shown before you start. Files come out square by default, which suits a product gallery. For a feed post, the [AI ad image generator](page:social-ad-photos) can turn a checked photo into a square ad image after this review. Different ages and builds are available. Pick the ones that match who you sell to.
sections.alt: Adult East Asian man checking the sleeve and hem of a plain gray hoodie in a fitting room.

sections.h2: Scale a Collection With a Batch
paras: When a drop has more than one color, run a batch so the saved look and the scene stay put, then review every file before it goes live.

Pair the on-model set with a flat photo from the [photo tools](page:photo-hub), a room scene from [lifestyle photos](page:lifestyle-photos), and a clean backdrop from the [background tool](page:change-background). A dye change belongs in a [color variant](page:tpl-color) only after you compare it with the real garment. [Fashion listings](page:ind-fashion-clothing) can use the same saved look across the collection.

sections.h2: How to Make Model Photos in 3 Simple Steps
paras: Upload a flat or hanger photo of the piece, with sleeves, hem, and collar in frame.

Pick an adult look and a scene that fit the piece. A short line can name the person, the pose, and the light. Save that look if you will need it again. The clothing comes from your photo, so you do not redesign the garment in words. A linen dress might be "a woman in her forties walking a sunny beach path, relaxed, late afternoon light." A hoodie might be "a young man leaning on a brick wall, hands in the front pocket, overcast daylight." Match the age and build to what you sell. Do not ask for a celebrity or a lookalike. Those requests may be refused.

Download the square file, or crop it for the channel, and compare neckline, length, print, and hardware with the real piece before you post. The [model photo tool](page:model-photos) is where that job starts.

faq.q: How does an on-model photo get made?
faq.a: You upload a flat or hanger photo, pick an adult look and a scene, and download a square image of the piece being worn. Then you compare it with the real garment.

faq.q: Can I put my own products on a generated person?
faq.a: Yes. The clothing or jewelry comes from your photo. You pick the person, the pose, and the light. Do not ask for a celebrity or a lookalike.

faq.q: Will the same person appear in all my photos?
faq.a: Yes, if you save the look and pick it again. If you describe someone new each time, the face can change. Repeat the age, hair, and build when you want the set to feel related.

faq.q: How close is this to a studio shoot?
faq.a: It shows the piece on a person in a scene you pick. It does not measure how a size will fit a shopper. Keep your size chart and measurements on the listing, and check neckline, length, print, and hardware.

faq.q: Can a catalog send these jobs through the API?
faq.a: Yes. A catalog can send products through the API and take the stills back. Each image is still 24 credits, and the cost is shown before the job starts.

faq.q: Do I need to say the person in the photo is generated?
faq.a: Check the current disclosure rule for the platform or marketplace where the image will appear. Rules differ by site and change, so follow the current one rather than an old screenshot.
Use a sharp, front-facing photo with the whole garment visible. Smooth wrinkles and use even light so fabric, print, and trim are easy to review.

faq.q: Can the image prove a garment fits?
faq.a: No. It cannot show how a size will sit on a shopper. Keep your size chart and measurements on the listing.

faq.q: How many credits does one on-model photo use?
faq.a: One photo uses 24 credits. The cost appears before the job starts, and a failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: Can I use jewelry as well as clothing?
faq.a: Yes. Start with a close photo that shows the clasp, stones, and chain, then check those details in the result.

faq.q: How should I review the result?
faq.a: Compare it with the real piece. Check the neckline, sleeve and hem length, print position, buttons, zipper side, clasp, stones, hands, and hairline.

faq.q: Can I run a whole color drop together?
faq.a: Yes. Save the look, run a batch across the colors, and review each file. A generated color may not match your dye, so compare it with the garment.
